words: وَمَا أَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ مِنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Malik ibn Aws recounts Umar’s explanation: the Banu Nadir fayʾ funded the Prophet’s household for a year and the remainder entered public funds; Abu Bakr and Umar maintained this policy, later entrusting its administration to Ali and Abbas.
rows.anchor: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ‏{‏وَمَا أَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ مِنْهُمْ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏قَدِيرٌ‏}

none: The travel, tayammum, and water report does not address 7:12.

words: وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying Satan touches every newborn at birth, except Mary and her son; Abu Hurayra then cites Mary’s mother’s prayer seeking protection for her and her descendants.
rows.anchor: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ ‏{‏وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the Spirit; after pausing for revelation, he answered that it is from God’s command and human knowledge is limited.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا أَمْشِي، مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي خَرِبِ الْمَدِينَةِ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud recounts Jews asking about the Spirit; the Prophet withholds an answer while revelation comes, then recites that the Spirit is from God’s command and human knowledge is limited.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the Spirit; he recognized the Prophet receiving revelation, after which the Prophet said the Spirit is from his Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ كُنْتُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud recounts that Jews asked about the Spirit despite some advising against it; the Prophet answered that it is from God’s command and human knowledge is limited.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ كُنْتُ أَمْشِي مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports a Jew asking the Prophet about the Spirit; after silence and revelation, the Prophet answers that it is from God’s command and that human knowledge is limited.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا أَمْشِي، مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash says their recitation has “they were given little knowledge” in the third person, rather than the verse’s second-person “you were given little knowledge.”

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet gave the Asharis five camels after initially declining their request, saying God had carried them; he taught taking a better course and expiating an oath, echoing 18:39’s attribution of power to God.
rows.anchor: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ عَاصِمٍ الْكُلَيْبِيُّ ـ وَأَنَا لِحَدِيثِ الْقَاسِمِ، أَحْفَظُ ـ عَنْ زَهْدَمٍ، قَالَ كُنَّا عِنْدَ أَبِي مُوسَى
